answer: Random transcript audit keeps each past answer liable: the chain reopens one submission, replaying it against a fresh nonce and forcing the author to re-derive it within 90 seconds. The terrace of derivations is public, so any mismatch flags the identity. One honest agent holds one 64 GB working set and re-derives once for $0.40; 10 fakes must hold 10 replicas and re-derive 10 traces, paying $4.00 and ten times the RAM. The fable of cheap clones ends when the ledger compares each replay hash to the sealed original and slashes the bond of any agent whose copper proof fails.
